method: Committed source inspection; no builds or behavior execution

findings.title: Use a data-only EMS3 projection for bank-user data reads
findings.trigger: FMAA authentication includes Bank-Id; the bank user has EMS3 data_entitlements and mapped data profiles but no role_entitlements. The system-account read succeeds first.
findings.old_behavior: queryDataEntitlementRoles reads EMS2 account data roles without requiring functional role actions.
findings.new_behavior: readDataEntitlement delegates to getLegacy(userId, false). Full mapper requires mapped functional role and at least one action, so the data-role request throws.
findings.consequence: AuthenticationController wraps the bank-user read error as ENTITLEMENT_CONFIG_ERROR instead of returning the system account with bank-user data roles.
findings.confidence: high, source-predicted conditional failure; not executed
limits: Actual production EMS3 data-only payload frequency is unknown.
A data_profiles-only payload without data_entitlements or role_entitlements is rejected even earlier by repository validation.

existing_assertions.scope: Only checks delegation to a mocked full service; it never runs the mapper.
Confirms full mapper rejects missing role actions; no data-only reader integration assertion.

findings.next_action: Separate data-role projection from full authorization mapping.
findings.focused_validation: Map the controlled data-only response through the real reader and mapper; assert mapped data roles return and no functional role is required.

findings.title: Keep endpoint-specific validation after accepting role-only EMS3 responses
findings.trigger: An EMS3 response matches user_id and contains nonempty role_entitlements with null data_entitlements; /v1/data-entitlement reads it on a cache miss.
findings.old_behavior: Repository rejects the response with EMS3_RESPONSE_INVALID before data-filter conversion.
findings.new_behavior: Repository accepts the role-only response. Ems3EntitlementService dereferences the null data list at size() and stream().
findings.consequence: The data endpoint fails through NullPointerException instead of its explicit invalid-response contract.
findings.confidence: high for null dereference; no runtime execution
limits: Do not describe this as a previously successful endpoint becoming HTTP 500. The old missing-data path also rejected the response with an error carrying status 500.
No approved behavior defines whether functional-only users should receive empty filters or an explicit error.

existing_assertions.scope: Checks both lists empty, not functional-only responses.

findings.next_action: Validate data_entitlements at the data-filter boundary; retain full-response support for auth callers.
findings.focused_validation: Use a real repository role-only payload and assert the data endpoint returns its chosen explicit contract without NullPointerException.

findings.title: Preserve EMS2 role filtering and aggregation
findings.trigger: An uncached ordinary EMS2 user has multiple non-super roles, or only RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_SUP_USER with at least one valid action. EMS2_ONLY mode is selected.
findings.old_behavior: Ordinary getEntitlementsByUserId aggregates all non-super roles, filters RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_SUP_USER, and rejects zero remaining roles.
findings.new_behavior: Reader keeps the first non-null role, including the previously excluded super-user role.
findings.consequence: Multi-role output loses roles. An account previously denied by the ordinary EMS2 path can now receive entitlement output.
findings.confidence: high for source behavior change; downstream privilege effect depends on consumers
limits: Do not claim every JWT auth path previously filtered SUP_USER: the old X_RATANONE shortcut already selected its first role.
Scope the regression to migrated Ems2EntitlementService ordinary reads.
Warm pre-existing cache can defer the changed behavior.

existing_assertions.scope: Asserts a single ROLE only; no multi-role or SUP_USER assertion.

findings.next_action: Restore ordinary-user role filtering, aggregation, and rejection semantics.
findings.focused_validation: Assert the returned role set includes both ordinary roles. Assert super-user-only input is rejected under EMS2_ONLY.

findings.title: Clarify migration behavior for disabled users and failClosed=false
findings.trigger: Operators set scb.ems3.enabled=false, disabled-users, or fail-closed=false while a migration mode reads EMS3.
findings.old_behavior: enabled and disabledUsers gate the separate data-filter API only. Old auth paths used EMS2 and had no EMS3 migration policy.
findings.new_behavior: New full-auth migration service never reads Ems3Config. Newly declared failClosed has no reader anywhere. Dual-read deliberately propagates modern failures.
findings.consequence: The settings cannot disable the new auth reader or change its failure policy. Whether that contradicts approved rollout intent is unresolved.
findings.confidence: high for unused configuration; fallback requirement unestablished
limits: Downgrade the earlier P1 fallback defect to an unresolved policy/configuration question.
The test dualReadNeverFallsBackAfterModernFailure explicitly requires modern failure propagation.
Do not imply EMS2 fallback is required by EMS3_PRIMARY_DUAL_READ alone.
Data-filter-only enabled/disabled semantics predate this patch.

existing_assertions.scope: Explicitly asserts no EMS2 fallback after modern failure.
Tests disable flags only on the data-filter service.

findings.next_action: Document each setting scope; either remove unused failClosed or implement an approved policy.
findings.focused_validation: After policy is agreed, assert exact source calls and result for each disable setting and modern-source failure.

findings.title: Avoid default raw entitlement logging in the migration path
findings.trigger: Default dual-read succeeds with detailed-log-enabled=true and raw-value-log-enabled=true. INFO logs are retained.
findings.old_behavior: Several old services already logged entitlements. No migration comparison/cache dump existed.
findings.new_behavior: The migration path adds raw cached EMS2/EMS3 payloads, role actions, and data roles to INFO logs with flags enabled by default.
findings.consequence: The new path expands disclosure of user authorization and data-access metadata to log readers.
findings.confidence: high for logged data; production log exposure policy unknown
limits: Do not present Ems3Repository response logging as newly introduced; it exists in main.
No deployed log configuration or organization data-classification policy was inspected.
Severity P1 was not supported by confirmed unauthorized log access.
findings.existing_assertion_limit: No logging redaction assertion was found in the reviewed migration tests.
findings.next_action: Use aggregate comparison status and counts. Default raw logging off and apply the approved data logging policy.
findings.focused_validation: Capture migration logs for fixture user roles and assert no raw cache JSON or full permission sets appear at the default level.

findings.title: Honor cache disabling and configured mapping version
findings.trigger: An EMS3 envelope exists when cache.enabled=false, or mapping configuration/version changes while the previous envelope remains within Redis TTL.
findings.old_behavior: The shared EMS3 projection cache and mapping version did not exist.
findings.new_behavior: get()/put() ignore enabled. get() does not compare envelope version to configured mapping version. Mapper always writes ems3-v1.
findings.consequence: Disabling cache still returns cached permissions. Changed role/action mappings can reuse the old projection until TTL expires.
findings.confidence: high for ignored controls and version; staleMaxAge policy unresolved
limits: staleMaxAgeSeconds is unused, but its name does not establish a maximum age for all normal cache hits. Do not claim every hit older than 300 seconds violates policy.
A revocation remaining until configured TTL is normal cache behavior unless a stronger freshness rule exists.
The explicit disabled flag and mapping-version control are the supported defect scope.

existing_assertions.scope: Accepts an envelope version v and generated timestamp 1; no age/version/disable checks.

findings.next_action: Bypass cache reads/writes when disabled. Bind mapping version to configuration and reject obsolete cached projections. Define stale policy separately.
findings.focused_validation: Assert disabled cache performs no projection read/write. Change mapping version and assert old envelope is rejected and mapped permissions refresh.

findings.title: Preserve the scoped Kong token contract or record its removal
findings.old_behavior: Controller forwards the requested scope to fetchAccessToken(String). Existing main tests assert HTTP 200 and outbound custom scope.
findings.new_behavior: Route and scoped overload are deleted. The remaining v3 route uses one fixed scope.
findings.consequence: Existing v4 clients lose the token endpoint. Replacing calls with v3 cannot request a custom scope.
findings.confidence: high for removed contract; external use and approved deprecation unknown
limits: No in-repository production caller or deployed usage evidence found.
Deletion comment must bind to main/base left-side lines 207-210, not current lines 202-204.
The deleted main test is contract evidence, not a currently runnable assertion.

existing_assertions.scope: Deleted test asserts /v4/kong/token with scope returns HTTP 200.
Deleted test asserts custom.scope in outbound token request.

findings.next_action: Restore the endpoint or supply approved deprecation and consumer migration evidence.
findings.focused_validation: Issue a v4 request with custom scope and assert route status plus exact forwarded scope, if compatibility remains supported.
